ruled_out.assertion: The aging widget interpolates ?days into a SQL interval literal
ruled_out.killed_by: The (int) cast at line 71 reduces the value to digits before it reaches the string; no non-numeric character survives it.

ruled_out.assertion: The invoice list interpolates ?sort and ?dir into ORDER BY
ruled_out.killed_by: Invoice::sortColumn (app/Models/Invoice.php:54-59) returns a member of the SORTABLE constant or its first element, and line 27 reduces dir to the literals 'asc' or 'desc'. Both are the allowlist that ORDER BY requires.

ruled_out.assertion: PdfRenderer builds a shell command with an unescaped $target
ruled_out.killed_by: $target is sprintf('%s/invoice-%d.pdf', $this->spoolDir, $invoice->id) at line 33: %d forces an integer and spoolDir is the constructor default at line 21. The two arguments that could carry request data are escapeshellarg'd, and $template is allowlisted at line 27.

ruled_out.assertion: The payment webhook signature check can be bypassed
ruled_out.killed_by: The HMAC is computed over t + '.' + the raw body with the configured secret and compared with hash_equals at line 45; the timestamp tolerance at line 33 bounds replay, a missing secret fails closed with 503 at line 40, and parseHeader has no branch that lets a malformed header through. This one is implemented correctly.

ruled_out.assertion: The failed-login audit line is a log-injection sink
ruled_out.killed_by: The email passes the 'email' validator at line 25 before it is logged, and it travels as a structured context array rather than being concatenated into the message, so the formatter escapes it. Both halves of the WEB-28 exculpation are present.

ruled_out.assertion: evaluation_series interpolates window_hours into a SQL interval
ruled_out.killed_by: window_hours arrives through Path<(String, i64)> (routes.rs:87), so a non-integer never reaches the handler, and routes.rs:96 clamps it to 1..720 before the call.

ruled_out.assertion: detail() loads a flag by primary key without a tenant filter
ruled_out.killed_by: The id is produced by flag_id_for_key (store.rs:37), which binds tenant_id as $1, so the value reaching load_flag is already scoped. The same pattern guards series() and archive().

ruled_out.assertion: The permissive CORS layer exposes the API to any origin
ruled_out.killed_by: AllowOrigin::any() is attached only to the probes router (main.rs:113-116), which carries /healthz and /buildinfo. The /api/v1 tree gets console_cors with an origin list from configuration (main.rs:101-111, 119).

ruled_out.assertion: queue_board interpolates the queue id into a raw SQL string
ruled_out.killed_by: int() at line 74 makes the value an integer or raises before the string is built; the organization predicate beside it is bound as %s.

ruled_out.assertion: scan_attachment builds a shell command from an attachment path
ruled_out.killed_by: stored_path (models.py:82-84) is ATTACHMENT_ROOT joined with uuid4().hex and the extension, and the extension can only be a member of ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS (forms.py:8, enforced at forms.py:28). No shell metacharacter can reach the command line - which is what distinguishes it from the sibling task in F-022.

ruled_out.assertion: ticket_export is the one view without @login_required
ruled_out.killed_by: LoginRequiredMiddleware refuses anonymous requests to anything outside PUBLIC_PATHS (middleware.py:17), it is registered in MIDDLEWARE after AuthenticationMiddleware (settings.py:51), and /tickets/export/ is not among the four public prefixes (settings.py:56-61). The missing decorator is a lost layer of defence in depth, not an open route.

ruled_out.assertion: PUBLIC_PATHS prefix matching lets a protected path be treated as public
ruled_out.killed_by: startswith would indeed make /healthz-anything public, but no url in config/urls.py begins with any of the four prefixes other than the intended ones. Recorded as a latent hazard for the next route added, not a present exposure.

ruled_out.assertion: ledger_app is granted UPDATE and DELETE on the audit log
ruled_out.killed_by: audit_log has RLS ENABLEd and FORCEd (002_rls.sql:12, 18) and carries only audit_read (SELECT) and audit_append (INSERT) policies. With RLS on and no policy for a command, PostgreSQL matches no rows, so the granted UPDATE and DELETE affect nothing. The grant is wider than the design note at 003_functions.sql:25-26 claims, and RLS is what makes that harmless.

ruled_out.assertion: account_balance_at concatenates an account id into dynamic SQL
ruled_out.killed_by: p_account_id is declared bigint in the signature (line 5), so PostgreSQL rejects anything that is not an integer before the body runs; p_asof is passed with USING.

ruled_out.assertion: account_balance_at sums entries with no tenant predicate
ruled_out.killed_by: The function is STABLE and not SECURITY DEFINER, so it executes as the invoker and the entries_read policy (002_rls.sql:64-67) applies to the EXECUTE. This is the contrast case for F-032: here the absence of a definer clause is what keeps it safe.

ruled_out.assertion: provision.sh calls rm -rf on a variable
ruled_out.killed_by: reset_dir is invoked only at lines 37 and 120, both with STAGE_DIR, a literal assigned at line 13. No caller passes anything derived from an argument.

ruled_out.assertion: SCRAM verifiers are committed in userlist.sample.txt
ruled_out.killed_by: The header (lines 1-7) documents them as throwaway values from a scratch cluster, the base64 payloads are visibly repeated padding rather than real digests, and provision.sh:101-105 writes the live /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt from the secret store on every deploy under umask 0177.

ruled_out.assertion: listNotes interpolates the limit into the LIMIT clause
ruled_out.killed_by: The only caller is recentNotes (app/actions/notes.ts:35), which passes the output of z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(200).default(50) (line 18). The value is an integer in 1..200 by the time it reaches the template.

ruled_out.assertion: The note page hands stored markup to dangerouslySetInnerHTML
ruled_out.killed_by: note.html is produced by renderNoteHtml (lib/policy.ts:66), which runs markdown-it with html: false so raw markup in the source is escaped, and overrides link_open (policy.ts:47-64) to rewrite any href whose scheme is outside http/https/mailto to '#'. The sanitiser is present and, as configured, does reject - it is not the inert kind. F-045 records the absent CSP behind it.

ruled_out.assertion: The share route makes a server-side request to a caller-supplied URL
ruled_out.killed_by: isAllowedShareTarget (lib/policy.ts:13-27) parses the candidate with the URL constructor, requires protocol https:, and compares parsed.hostname - not the raw string - against a build-time list. hostname is the right field: userinfo and port tricks such as https://hooks.allowed.example@evil.example resolve to evil.example and fail the check. The authorization defect on that route is F-040.

ruled_out.assertion: middleware.ts leaks the user id in the x-nw-user response header
ruled_out.killed_by: The header is set on the response to the same caller whose cookie already contains userId in clear (lib/session.ts:27), so nothing is disclosed that the recipient did not send. It is a no-op rather than a leak - the header would have to be set on the forwarded request to serve its apparent purpose.

ruled_out.assertion: A JWT signing key is committed in appsettings.json
ruled_out.killed_by: The adjacent comment identifies it as the RFC 7515 appendix A.1 worked-example octets, and the code reads Jwt:SigningKey (TokenService.cs:20 and 41) while this key is stored under Jwt:FixtureSigningKey - a different key, read by nothing. The real defect on that path is F-046, which makes the signing key irrelevant.

ruled_out.assertion: Production CORS allows every origin
ruled_out.killed_by: Program.cs:49 builds the console policy from Cors:PublicOrigins, which is the single console origin on line 29. I grepped for AllowedOrigins: no code reads it. It is a dead key that looks like a wildcard policy and is not one.

ruled_out.assertion: The firmware download joins a path segment into a filesystem path
ruled_out.killed_by: The channel parameter binds to the FirmwareChannel enum (Models/FleetModels.cs:9-15); ASP.NET model binding rejects the request when the segment does not parse to a member, and channel.ToString() can only produce a member name or digits. Neither can contain a separator or a dot segment.

ruled_out.assertion: The probe CORS policy allows any origin on the API
ruled_out.killed_by: The named policy is applied only at Program.cs:64 and 68, to /healthz and /version. It is never the default policy and app.MapControllers() takes the console policy (line 70).

ruled_out.assertion: Device registration binds the request body onto the entity, exposing IsFactoryUnlocked
ruled_out.killed_by: The parameter binds to the DeviceRegistration record (line 117), whose only members are Serial and Model, and the Device is constructed field by field at lines 79-85 with TenantId taken from the token. IsFactoryUnlocked is not reachable from the body - this is the DTO allowlist that WEB-06 asks for.
